resources.string: Starts the A/C at a level that fits the car\'s temperature.
Sign in with your BYD account and pick your car. Password and PIN stay encrypted on this phone.
Your password and PIN stay encrypted on this phone and are only sent to BYD.
BYD server (set automatically from the country)

Unlocks and starts the car when your phone gets within the start distance, or when a beacon in the car is strong enough (above). It runs again only after you get further than the re-arm distance and the minimum minutes have passed.
It always unlocks first. Start car and A/C on put the car in remote mode, and BYD then asks for the key before you can drive, even after another unlock. To drive without the key, choose Unlock.
Phone location can be off by several metres. Anyone holding your phone can trigger it.
Runs once you get past the re-arm distance after an auto-start. It\'s skipped if the car moved, so driving off doesn\'t run it. Arming by trusted Wi-Fi doesn\'t run it either.
How often to measure your distance to the car. Shorter reacts sooner but uses more battery. Default 5. Applies when you start monitoring.

While GPS monitoring is on, a strong signal from one of these networks arms the distance trigger, as if you had walked away. A weak signal, like at the car, is ignored. Nothing is sent to the car, and the car is never started while you are connected to one of these networks, however weak the signal. Connect to the network, then tap Add current Wi-Fi.
Default −70. Tap Add current Wi-Fi in the house and again at the car: each shows the signal there. Pick a value between the two.

Start car reads the cabin temperature and starts the A/C at the matching range. When the car has no cabin reading (it has none while asleep), it uses the outside temperature at the car from a weather service. Changes are saved straight away.
Each range starts where you set it and the one below ends there. Moving a border past another moves that one along, so the ranges never overlap.
Sends what you write, with the app\'s state and about the last day of its log, to your report webhook. Never your password, PIN, email or locations.
What happened? For example: I was next to the car and it showed 151 km.
Add the report webhook address in Settings first.
Report a problem sends reports here as JSON: your description, the time, the phone and app state, settings and about the last day of the log. It must start with https://.
Nothing yet. Each action shows here with what triggered it: the app, the widget, Bluetooth, the distance or walking away.
Combine steps into one button. Custom actions can go on the widget or run on auto-start.

Keep a small beacon in the car. Auto-start fires when a beacon\'s signal reaches its strength, or when you\'re within the start distance, whichever comes first. Use a beacon that broadcasts all the time (iBeacon or Eddystone); a car\'s own Bluetooth usually can\'t be used.
None yet. Tap Scan, then Add next to your beacon.
Tap Scan to look for beacons around you. The strongest is listed first, so hold the beacon next to the phone.
While monitoring. Nonstop notices you within a second or two. Less often saves battery, but the car can start up to that many seconds after you arrive. Applies straight away.
Starts the car when the signal is %1$d dBm or stronger. Below %2$d dBm the beacon counts as away, which makes auto-start ready for your next arrival.
%1$d dBm: strong enough to start the car
%1$d dBm: too weak to start the car
Not heard for %1$d s. Is the beacon on and close enough?
Not listening, so only the value can be changed.
The default. Calibrate beside the car to set the right strength.
To calibrate, put the beacon in the car, stand where the car should start (for example beside the driver\'s door), keep the phone still and tap Calibrate.
middle reading %1$d dBm, range %2$d to %3$d dBm, %4$d readings
Calibrated just now: %1$s. Suggested %2$d dBm, 3 dB weaker than here, so this spot triggers reliably. Tap Save to keep it.
Calibrated %1$s: %2$s. Set 3 dB weaker than the middle reading.
Set by hand %1$s. Calibration had suggested %2$d dBm (%3$s).
BYD Arrival can start your car as you walk up to it, using your phone\'s location and the car\'s parked position.
When you come within the start distance, the app unlocks the car and starts it.
Once you\'re past the re-arm distance, it\'s ready for your next return. It can\'t fire again until then.
The car never starts while your phone is on a Wi-Fi network you list in Settings.
Start with these values and adjust them after trying it. You can change them later in Settings.
Phone location can be several metres off, so very short distances may not work reliably.
Must be further than the start distance. The app raises it if needed.
Stops it starting again if you walk past the car soon after.
Starts within %1$d m, re-arms beyond %2$d m, and starts at most once every %3$d min.
Your car will unlock and start for real when you walk up to it. It has to see you walk away first, so turning it on beside the car does nothing. To turn it off, tap Stop in its notification.
Android will ask for location access. Choose Allow all the time so it works with the screen off.
Auto-start needs location access. You can start it later in Settings.

In Israel the car is never this far away, so a reading beyond this distance means the car\'s position or your phone\'s location was read wrong. The reading is ignored and tracking restarts: the car\'s position is read from BYD again and your location readings start afresh, at most every 5 minutes. Israel is about 420 km long, so 450 catches more wrong readings.
Restart tracking beyond (km from the car, 100–5000)
For trips abroad: pauses tracking, so there\'s no auto-start, no requests to BYD and no restarts for long distances, until you switch it off. Widget buttons still work.
Tap a button to control your car
One-tap start, lock, unlock and trunk
